The strip Jacobian is one. For a transverse crossing, its displacement in t is O(epsilon) and the roof height there is epsilon h(t0)+O(epsilon²), even at a polygonal kink. The speed identity follows by taking the determinant of the edge vector and the tangent to the cut, giving the exact section atom normalization.
Direct differentiation gives the three partials using sum E_l=2Psi+product f=8+product f. Counting the total area once in the double sector yields beta_s=alpha_i+alpha_j−C/(2k).

Vertex shifts parallel to the other incident edge preserve the other two boundary lines and have signed roof derivatives proportional to 1−t and t. Any end wedges have quadratic area and are separated from the section crossings. The strict triangle inequality gives an interior differentiable local maximum, so the two moments vanish separately.

The kernel has second derivative −delta_t and endpoint slopes equal to the two moments up to sign. Integrating the outer constant densities yields the two negative quadratic branches, and interpolation with second derivative −beta_s yields the middle branch.

All f_l lie strictly between zero and two. The positive discriminant complement proves alpha_i,alpha_j>0. Dividing the middle formula by z(1−z) gives a strictly minimized A/z+B/(1−z), with one minimizing peak. The outer pieces and both seam peaks are strictly negative.
